doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Jump Town and the Ventura band
title: Meeting at Jump Town and Jackie's first sitting in
summary: Love at first note; Roy's George Davis Quartet at Jump Town, Jackie brought in by a tenor player, and the club owner hires her for weekends. They then begin vocalese after hearing Buddy Stewart and Dave Lambert.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So was it love at first note for you guys?
No. Oh yes, love at first note. But not at first sight.
She was much too young for me.
Well Roy’s seven years old than I am, so at that point when I was about 18, 17, 18 years old—

No. I met him when I was 17 I believe it was. And he had another girlfriend, and I was just this little naive girl from Milwaukee you know. So I don’t think I attracted his attention that much. But then he did like working with me I believe.

Here’s what happened. A friend of mine brought her in to the club, Jump Town, it was early ‘47, on the west end of Chicago. Dave Garroway was looking for sponsors. Jump Town was his first sponsor. He talked up the club. He talked it up, talked it up, the place starts to boom. And this friend of mine, a tenor player, brought Jackie in to hear our quartet. I was working with the George Davis Quartet. It was alto, piano, bass and drums. And this tenor player said, “hey let her sing, she’s really good.” And I says, “naaa, don’t be bringing your girls in here, they’ll ask me to play in the key of X, something that I don’t know anyway.”

Piano players never like to play for girl singers, because half the time they don’t know what key they sing and they don’t know what tune they want to do, and that sort of thing. So they’re sort of negative about it in general.

So I said no, no, no deal. We went to the bar and libations, and Vete [Bob Anderson] said, “ah come on, she’s good.” She’ll — okay. She sang “Happiness is Just a Thing Called Joe.” And I happened to have loved that song because hearing Frances Wayne sing it with Woody Herman’s band, a Neal Hefti arrangement. I said God, that’s great. Okay. And she sang that. The club owner was there that night, and he came up to us and said, “you guys need a singer for Friday and Saturday.” Okay.

And that’s how we started working together. But I was just the girl singer. I mean we didn’t do things together in the beginning. I was just singing ballads and uptempos and do a few tunes every set. And the group was quite a good group. And then eventually as we went along, suddenly we heard, let’s see Buddy Stewart and Dave Lambert with Gene Krupa. We had heard it around that time. They did some records where they used their voices singing together, with the instruments of the orchestra, and it was vocalese all the way, no lyrics, and we said hey that’s great.
